v0.5.0

Added

  • (treepplr#12) Add tp_runtime_options
  • (treepplr#13) tp_run(n_runs) to run multiple sweeps/runs
  • (treepplr#13) tp_run(n_processes) to run MCMC or SMC in parallel using n cores
  • (treepplr#13) tp_compile_methods() to find available methods
  • (treepplr#14) Tim and Stenio as package authors in DESCRIPTION.
  • (treepplr#31) At the end of a run, tp_run() now prints a summary with runtime information and output directories/files.
  • (treepplr#31) New argument wide in tp_parse_smc() and tp_parse_mcmc() to choose between wide (standard in other software) and long (good for plotting) format. Default = TRUE.

Changed

  • (treepplr#12) Change “compiled_model” to “sampler” (temporary)
  • (treepplr#13) Updated the documentation
  • (treepplr#14) treepplr package installation should be done with pak::pak because devtools::install_github will soon be deprecated.
  • (treepplr#30) Updated roxygen documentation for tp_parse_smc() and tp_parse_mcmc(). Changed their output objects to tidy data frames.
  • (treepplr#31) tp_run() now returns a tidy data frame (in wide format by default) instead of a list. It automatically calls tp_parse_smc() or tp_parse_mcmc(), depending on the inference method and model passed to tp_compile(). For models without a parser yet (e.g., models that return trees), it returns the path to the output JSON file along with a message.
  • (treepplr#31) tp_parse_smc() and tp_parse_mcmc() now take a character vector with the path(s) to the JSON output file(s) instead of the list returned by tp_run().
  • (treepplr#31) tp_mcmc_convergence() and tp_smc_convergence() now accept data frames in either long or wide format.

Deprecated

  • (treepplr#12) all references to n_runs have been remove

Removed

Fixed

  • (treepplr#12) Always check if tpplc is installed before calling it
  • (treepplr#12) tp_compile_options update for new --help format
  • (treepplr#30) tp_parse_smc() and tp_parse_mcmc() now parse per-particle/iteration with explicit indices and (for SMC) join weights by index using left_join(..., by = "particle") instead of relying on positional recycling, which is the default behavior of data.frame() when handling vectors of different lengths.
